notes: This is one typewritten sheet carrying numerous pen corrections and additions. The top-centre page number is 1. The lower-left pencil archive number is also 1. The upper-right note reads 9/74 and Envoyé par Grothendieck, in a hand visibly different from the main corrections. No total page count appears on this sheet.

The title is Esquisse d'une théorie des Gr-Catégories and the byline is par Mme Hoang Xuan Sinh. The introduction says that the author intends to present the detailed work shortly as a doctoral thesis. Both reference slots are drawn empty square brackets.

The paragraph defines the categories under discussion via a binary tensor operation associative and unital up to prescribed isomorphism; a handwritten insertion adds the groupoid requirement before the condition that every object be invertible. These are statements encountered in reading, not proofs checked in this run.

The first example uses loops and homotopy classes of homotopies, with the distinct singular d'homotopie followed by plural d'homotopies retained. The first loop concatenation sentence says that the operation is associative only à homotopie près. The note in the left margin relates this example to the following Hopf-space variant and includes a definite Omega superscript 1.

The Hopf-space letter was inspected at all five typed occurrences. The composite glyph is not clean enough to establish its identity or a blackboard font. The handwritten margin G does not by itself settle the typed glyph. The first occurrence therefore explicitly carries G|E|K, and later occurrences follow G under the recurring-glyph rule.

The second example discusses F-torsors and Baer composition. The ink says only faisceau at that point; no additional group or commutativity qualification has been supplied. It then names invertible Modules over a locally ringed space/topos and the special case F equal to the units of the underlined structure sheaf.

The third example uses the full subcategory of equivalences in underlined Hom(A,A) with a small handwritten is qualifier, then mentions a general 2-category and a not necessarily commutative sheaf of groups. The page ends after the amended phrase (ou un topos), with an old X separately cancelled.

All agreed prose was checked directly in the two halves. No OCR, text-recognition service, PDF text layer, outside source, other scan page, or other reader output was used. Twenty tight crops were made once each from the original full-resolution whole image, with only PIL crop, LANCZOS resize, autocontrast and sharpening. Neither whole nor halves were reopened.

No standalone diagrams or substantive drawings occur. The northeast pen arrow is the attachment mark of the left marginal note and is transcribed with that note. Single underlines and insertion attachment lines were distinguished: localement, plus généralement, c'est un groupoïde, and ponctué par x in X have caret/leader attachments, not semantic underlines.

The reading begins with scanpage 2 and mspage 1. The extra cotefile marker in supplied C was omitted as instructed for a nonfirst scan; this is editorial framing, not an ink-derived textual disagreement. Handwritten markup differences alone are not counted as witness reading changes.
No mathematical claim was proved, disproved, computed or independently rechecked in this run. Formula inspections in this report are visual transcription checks only.
